llms.summary: Nefo is a free, open-source (AGPLv3) control panel for one Linux server: websites, SSL, databases, one-click apps, backups and a security check from a web interface. It is a single program that uses about {ram} of RAM, and nothing is sent home.
facts: Runs on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 and Debian 12 and 13, tested on x86-64; built for a VPS with 1 GB of RAM.
Install as root on a fresh server: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/nefocp/nefo/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash`
The panel itself uses about {ram} of RAM, measured on a live server.
{apps} apps in the app store; the interface in {languages} languages.
Free software under the GNU AGPLv3. No account, no telemetry, every feature free.
Not included by design: a mail server, a DNS server, several servers in one panel.

home.h1: A free control panel for your Linux server
home.lead: Websites, SSL, databases, {apps} one-click apps, backups and a security check in one web interface. Nefo is a single program that uses about {ram} of RAM. Every feature is free, and nothing is sent home.
home.cmdTitle: as root, on a fresh server

tour.lead: Taken on a test server with eight websites and two Docker apps; the week of load and traffic history is sample data. Pick a page, and switch the window between light and dark.

websites.label: Websites
websites.caption: Every site with its type, PHP version, certificate, visits and backups: PHP, static, WordPress, Node.js, Docker apps and reverse proxies in one list.
websites.alt: The Websites page: eight websites with their type, PHP version, certificate, visits and backups

site.label: Site settings
site.caption: One drawer per website: domain, PHP, SSL, access, Git, backups, logs and security, without leaving the list.
site.alt: The settings drawer of one website, with its domain, PHP, SSL, access, Git, backups, logs and security tabs

apps.label: App store
apps.caption: {apps} apps by category. PHP apps go into a website with their own database; Docker apps get a website of their own.
apps.alt: The App store page: apps by category, each with a one-click install button

databases.label: Databases
databases.caption: MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Redis on one page, each database linked to its website, with its size, access, import and export.
databases.alt: The Databases page: MariaDB and PostgreSQL databases with their website, size and access, and Redis

backups.label: Backups
backups.caption: Copies on this server and on SFTP, S3 or Google Drive, schedules with retention, restore after a checksum check.
backups.alt: The Backups page: backups of websites, databases, folders and apps, kept on this server and on SFTP

security.label: Security check
security.caption: 22 checks of the server, each with what was found and a link to the fix.
security.alt: The Security check page: 22 checks of the server, each with its result and a link to the fix

software.label: Software
software.caption: What is installed, what each part costs in RAM and disk, and what you can add or remove.
software.alt: The Software page: the web server and PHP versions, with the memory each one needs

features.lead: Install only what you use. The menu hides what isn't installed, and every part can be removed again.

web.h3: PHP, Node.js, Python and Java sites, or a proxy to any address
web.p: Each website gets its own Linux user, its own PHP settings and a free certificate, on Nginx, Apache or OpenLiteSpeed.
ticks: PHP 5.6 to 8.6 side by side, a version per site
Let's Encrypt certificates that renew themselves, wildcard through Cloudflare DNS, or your own
SFTP locked to the site's folder, with a password or SSH keys
Clone a site, make a WordPress staging copy, deploy from Git on every push
Import from a cPanel full backup, or a site archive and SQL dump
web.alt: The settings drawer of a website in Nefo

db.h3: MariaDB or MySQL, PostgreSQL and Redis
db.p: Databases are linked to their website, so its backup includes them. Upgrades make a dump first and roll back if something fails.
ticks: MariaDB 11.4, 11.8 or 12.3 LTS, or MySQL 8.4, and a switch between them with the data
PostgreSQL 15 to 19, with remote access per database over TLS
Remote access per database, only from the addresses you allow
Adminer and phpMyAdmin, reachable only through the panel's sign-in
A Redis key browser, and Memcached
db.alt: The list of databases in Nefo, each linked to its website

bak.h3: Backups to S3, SFTP or Google Drive, encrypted if you like
bak.p: Websites, databases, folders and Docker apps, by hand or every day or week, with the number of copies to keep.
ticks: S3-compatible storage: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO
SFTP with the host key pinned; Google Drive with access only to the files Nefo creates
Encryption with your passphrase (scrypt and AES-256-GCM) before a copy leaves the server
Restore checks the SHA-256 first; a new server finds the backups on a storage and creates the websites again
bak.alt: The list of backups in Nefo, with where each copy is stored

sec.h3: A security check of the whole server
sec.p: 22 quick checks, on demand or once a day, each with what was found and a link to the fix. Nothing keeps running between checks.
ticks: SSH, firewall, pending updates, databases or Redis open to the internet, Docker ports that skip ufw
Files reachable over HTTP, certificates, PHP settings
Web application firewall (ModSecurity with OWASP rules), rate limits, blocked addresses, country blocking
File lock that keeps a website's code read-only for PHP; malware scanner with quarantine
Alerts for SSH sign-ins and bursts of failed logins
sec.alt: The results of the security check in Nefo

sw.h3: Install and remove software from one page
sw.p: Each part shows its RAM and disk cost before you install it. Removal is refused while a website or database still uses it, and data is kept unless you confirm.
ticks: Web server, PHP 5.6 to 8.6 with the ionCube Loader, MariaDB or MySQL, PostgreSQL
Redis, Memcached, Node.js, Python, Java (OpenJDK 17, 21, 25), Composer, WP-CLI
Docker with Compose projects, checked for privileged containers and public ports
Web application firewall and ClamAV, only if you want them
sw.alt: The Software page of Nefo, with the memory each part needs

apps.lead: PHP apps go into a website with their own database. Docker apps run behind a website of their own, which stays closed until their default logins are replaced.

install.h2: One command on a fresh server
install.lead: The installer sets up one program and a systemd service. Then you choose the rest of the software on a setup page.

steps.title: Get a fresh server
steps.text: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 or 26.04, or Debian 12 or 13, on x86-64. Built for a VPS with 1 GB of RAM.

steps.title: Run the installer as root
steps.text: It checks the release's Ed25519 signature and checksum, installs /usr/local/bin/nefo and a systemd service, and picks a random port and a secret path.

steps.title: Sign in and choose your software
steps.text: Open the address it prints and sign in with the one-time password. On the setup page, pick the web server, PHP versions and database, with their RAM and disk cost.

compare.lead: The differences in short. Other panels vary; the right column is what you often find.

rows.label: Sign-in page
rows.us: Only on a secret path; every other address answers 404
rows.them: On a well-known port and path

rows.label: Updates
rows.us: Signed with Ed25519 and checked before they install

rows.label: Lock-out guards for firewall and SSH

faq.lead: More in the documentation and its FAQ.

items.a: Yes. Every feature is in the one version, under the AGPLv3. There is no account to create and nothing is sent home.

items.q: Which systems does it run on?
items.a: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04, and Debian 12 and 13, on x86-64, each tested on a fresh server. It is built for a VPS with 1 GB of RAM.

items.q: How much memory does it use?
items.a: About {ram} of RAM for the panel itself, measured on a live server running Nefo {version}. The software you install next to it, such as the web server, PHP and the database, uses its own.

items.q: Can I move my websites from another panel?
items.a: Yes: from a cPanel full backup (files, databases with their users and passwords, certificates, cron jobs), or from a site archive and an SQL dump made by any other panel.

items.q: Does it include a mail server?
items.a: No, on purpose: a mail server needs a lot of care and memory. Websites send mail through your SMTP provider, and the DNS page sets up MX, SPF and DMARC for Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Zoho or Cloudflare Email Routing.
Nefo is beta. It is in daily use on test servers but has not had an outside security audit yet. Keep backups, and try it first on a server you can rebuild.

items.q: Which languages does the interface speak?
items.a: English, Vietnamese, Chinese, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Indonesian. The browser loads only the language in use.
Run nefo update on the server. Every release is signed with Ed25519, and the signature is checked before the update installs.
